hints: Focus on the total electron pairs around the central atom, both bonding pairs and lone pairs, because that controls the shape.
Count for nitrogen in $\text{NH}_3$: it has 3 bonds plus 1 lone pair, while boron in $\text{BF}_3$ has 3 bonds and no lone pair.
Compare each pair for same numbers of bonds and lone pairs, and look for the one pair where the lone pair count makes the geometries split.
walkthrough:
**Recall how shape is decided**

Think VSEPR theory with me. Shape depends on the number of bonding pairs and lone pairs on the central atom.

Lone pairs repel more strongly, so even one extra lone pair can change the shape completely.

**Check the pairs that match**

$\text{BeCl}_2$ has 2 bonds, 0 lone pairs, so linear. $\text{CO}_2$ also has 2 bonds, 0 lone pairs, so linear too.

$$\text{2 bonding, 0 lone} \rightarrow \text{linear, } 180^{\circ}$$

**Check the tetrahedral and bent pairs**

$\text{CH}_4$ and $\text{NH}_4^+$ both have 4 bonds and 0 lone pairs, so both are tetrahedral.

$\text{SCl}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ both have 2 bonds and 2 lone pairs, so both are bent (V-shaped).

**Spot the different pair**

$\text{NH}_3$ has 3 bonds plus 1 lone pair, so it is trigonal pyramidal. $\text{BF}_3$ has 3 bonds and 0 lone pairs, so it is trigonal planar.

$$\text{NH}_3: 3+1 \rightarrow \text{pyramidal} \quad \text{vs} \quad \text{BF}_3: 3+0 \rightarrow \text{planar}$$

Same number of atoms attached, but different lone pairs, so different shapes.

options.A: Both are linear with bond angle 180 degrees. Be has 2 bonding pairs and no lone pairs, and C in CO2 also has effectively 2 regions and no lone pairs, so shapes are the same.
options.B: Both are tetrahedral. C in CH4 and N in NH4+ each have 4 bonding pairs and no lone pairs, so the extra H+ does not change the shape.
options.C: Shapes are different. NH3 is trigonal pyramidal due to 3 bonds plus 1 lone pair, while BF3 is trigonal planar with 3 bonds and no lone pair. This is the only pair that does not match.
options.D: Both are bent (V-shaped, non-linear). S in SCl2 and O in H2O each have 2 bonds plus 2 lone pairs, giving a similar bent geometry with about 104 to 109 degrees.
